note: Absolute pixel coords are only valid at the calibration_resolution/UI-scale above. window_relative fractions (0-1) are relative to the outer window box and should be more portable across resolutions -- multiply by the window's current w/h and add its x0,y0 to get absolute coords at a new resolution.

name.note: Bottom edge extended from 130 to 140 -- descender depth (e.g. the tail of 'y') varies slightly between renders, and 130 clipped it in at least one real capture ('Kryxon' lost its descender) despite fitting with only ~2px to spare in another ('Bardiyan'). 140 stays safely clear of the type_subtype row starting at y=144-145.

type_subtype.note: Left edge deliberately excludes the type-icon badge (verified user-supplied box, calibrated against a Str/Dex mercenary where the icon shape had previously leaked stray OCR characters into the type text).

level.note: The 'Lvl NN' box in the same header row as type_subtype, immediately to its right. Calibrated from a user-supplied CTRL+PRTSC screenshot with the box hand-drawn around it (Lorakna, the Profuse, Lvl 83) -- the drawn rectangle was measured directly (exact-color pixel bounding box), not eyeballed. Position confirmed stable (same absolute box cleanly frames the text with no re-adjustment) across 7 more real CTRL+PRTSC screenshots spanning Lvl 66-83, so this isn't fit to one mercenary's subtype-text width. CAUTION: those calibration screenshots are CTRL+PRTSC captures, not mss -- per this project's own documented capture-method color/border mismatch (see AI_RAMBLINGS.md), they were used ONLY to find and sanity-check this pixel box and are not stored as project test data. The box's real-world reliability under actual mss captures (crop position AND OCR) is unconfirmed until a real mss capture with this region wired in exists.

rucksack.note: Quadrant position is fixed; the item occupying each slot varies per encounter and must be identified via icon matching, not assumed from the slot name.

grid.note: Fixed 6-row x 5-column icon slot grid inside the supports panel, measured directly from real captures rather than eyeballed. Row/column pixel positions are IDENTICAL across every real capture checked (57 different real 5-icon rows across many different captures/mercenaries all produced byte-identical column boundaries; the 6 row-divider positions were likewise identical, modulo a few false-positive detections from icon content near a boundary, across every capture sampled). Rows correspond 1:1 to the same 6 slots as the `skills` region, in the same top-to-bottom order (row 0 = first/Primary skill slot, etc.) -- a mercenary with fewer real skills just leaves the extra rows blank, same panel size regardless (`supports.png` is always exactly 356x369px post-crop). Columns fill left-to-right starting at 0; a skill with fewer than 5 real supports leaves the remaining columns on its row blank. Absolute values here are RAW (pre-`capture_pipeline.py` INSET), same convention as every other region in this file -- `columns[c]` gives that column's {x0,x1} and `rows[r]` gives that row's {y0,y1} (already trimmed a few px in from the row's divider lines on both sides, tight around the actual icon+tier-badge content, not the full 58px row band) -- combine `columns[c]` x with `rows[r]` y to get one cell's absolute box. A cell being blank (no support in that slot) can't be known from `definitions/` data alone -- an equipped support count varies per real encounter within its skill's `SupportCountTier` range -- so occupancy has to be checked against the actual pixels (e.g. compare a cell's brightness/variance to a known-blank cell) once this grid is wired into capture code, not assumed from data.
